{{short description|English-born American mathematician}}
'''Aubrey John Kempner''' (22 September 1880, in [[Greater London]], [[England]] – 18 November 1973, in [[Boulder, Colorado]]) was an English-born American mathematician, known for the [[Kempner function]] and the [[Kempner series]].

Aubrey Kempner received in 1911 his PhD with the dissertation ''Über das [[Waring problem|Waringsche Problem]] und einige Verallgemeinerungen'' under [[Edmund Landau]] at the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|12376}}</ref>
He then went to the US and taught at the [[University of Illinois]] and from 1925 at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder]], where he remained until 1949 and from 1944 to 1949 was chair of the mathematics department. From 1950 he also taught at the [[University of Colorado School of Medicine|Colorado School of Medicine]] and at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] in Boulder.

Kempner's research was mainly in [[number theory]] and the theory of calculating the center of mass of a region defined by [[polynomial equation]]s. In his honor the mathematics faculty of the University of Colorado at Boulder established the Kempner Colloquium. In the years 1937 and 1938 he was president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>[http://www.maa.org/history/presidents/kempner.html Kempner] at the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]] website</ref>
